minutes.headline: Superintendent corrected a budget math error, lowering the FY27 deficit; athletic trainer cuts left undecided
minutes.summary: The School Committee heard the superintendent publicly correct a budget calculation error that had inflated the reported FY27 deficit, approved several transfers, donations, and a grant-funded field trip, and declined to pursue outsourcing custodial and facilities staff. The bulk of the meeting was spent debating whether to cut the athletic trainer position in favor of a cheaper EMT model as part of the FY27 restoration/override budget; the committee tabled that decision and set a rough override target without resolving it.

what_happened.line: The superintendent told the committee a math error had overstated the FY27 budget deficit and gave a corrected, lower figure.
The committee tabled a decision on cutting the athletic trainer position for a cheaper EMT staffing model, with at least one member opposed to tabling.
The committee decided not to pursue outsourcing custodial and facilities staff and will not revisit it on the agenda.
The committee set a rough FY27 override target without restoring full athletic staffing, leaving that question open.
The superintendent's office agreed to begin producing a quarterly HR staffing report for the committee.

why_it_matters: The corrected deficit changes the size of the gap the FY27 override is meant to close, which affects what residents are eventually asked to fund.
The still-unresolved athletic trainer vs. EMT question affects coverage for student athletes and is tied to the override ask.
Custodial and facilities jobs stay in-house rather than being outsourced, the outcome raised repeatedly in public comment.
watch_next: Legislative advocacy letter, aimed to be finalized and sent by March 18
A final decision on the FY27 athletic trainer/athletic director staffing structure, still tabled

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on every vote, transfer, and figure through the facilities report — donations, the SOA and special-ed transfers, and the Minute Man field trip costs all match (with a few pure digit-grouping/name misreadings from the captions). The most important divergence is structural: the official minutes contain no mention at all of the FY27 athletic trainer/athletic director staffing discussion — including the vote to table it, its no vote, the $9,000 EMT proposal, the $42,886 restoration cost, and the override-share figures — while conversely the official minutes credit "TJ Laughlin" with catching the deficit error and name several guests (Emily Young, Tim Santry, Norman Yvon) that our minutes omit entirely.
